name: Medium swept-back taper
summary: A medium-length men's cut with a longer top brushed back over neatly tapered sides and nape, without a disconnected undercut.
intro: The defining shape is a medium top that can be directed backward, paired with sides that shorten gradually around the ears and nape.
The taper can be cut with scissors or clippers and kept soft; this is not a skin fade or a disconnected undercut. A natural part may appear when the hair is swept back.
The brushed-back finish is a styling choice. The underlying cut can also be worn with a loose side part or left more natural.

variations.name: Soft swept-back taper
variations.description: Keeps the side transition subtle and the top loose, with natural movement rather than a sharp glossy finish.

variations.name: Defined swept-back taper
variations.description: Uses a clearer side part and light styling product to hold the top back while preserving a tapered, connected outline.

consultation.intro: Agree on top length, side length, and how visible the taper should be; show the barber how far back you want the front directed.
questions: How much length should remain at the front and crown?
Should the sides be scissor-tapered or gradually clipped, and how close should they finish?
Do you want a visible side part or a relaxed, natural sweep?
How much daily blow-drying or product are you comfortable using?
consultation.sampleRequest: “Keep a medium length on top so I can brush it back, taper the sides and nape softly with no skin fade or undercut, and leave enough movement that it does not look stiff.”

considerations: The brushed-back finish usually needs enough length at the front and some styling direction; a shorter fringe will not sweep the same way.
Straight or wavy hair can follow the shape with different amounts of product, while curlier textures may need more length or a softer outline.
A strong disconnect changes the silhouette into an undercut, so ask for a connected taper if that is not the intended result.
